stories.headline: Delhi High Court Refuses To Interfere With Centre's Decision To Close Kartarpur Corridor Following Pahalgam Terror Attack
stories.title: Delhi High Court Refuses To Interfere With Centre's Decision To Close Kartarpur Corridor Following Pahalgam Terror Attack
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'terror attack' in title weight 84
article_sentences: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday refused to entertain a plea seeking opening of the Kartarpur Corridor, a route connecting Gurdwara Dera Baba Nanak in Gurdaspur, Punjab, to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur, Pakistan.

A division bench comprising Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma noted that the decision was taken by the Government of India to close the corridor from May 07, 2025, following the Pahalgam terror attack.
The plea was filed by NGO Paardarshita Public Welfare Foundation seeking opening of the corridor for Sikh pilgrims as they have great faith in the gurudwara in Kartarpur, Pakistan.

The Court said that the decision to close the corridor was taken by the government of India in the interest of the citizens and thus, in view of the policy decision, there was no reason to cause any interference in the same in extraordinary writ jurisdiction.
However, noting that the representation of the petitioner was pending with the authorities, the Court said that it trusts and hopes that the respondents shall look into the same.
“With the aforesaid liberty, the petition stands disposed of,” the Court said.

stories.headline: Assessment of flood damages: High level Inter Ministerial team arrives in JK, to visit multiple flood hit districts
stories.title: Assessment of flood damages: High level Inter Ministerial team arrives in JK, to visit multiple flood hit districts
stories.summary: Rajouri, Nov 25: For on spot assessment of the situation after flash floods, a high level Inter Ministerial team from Government of India has arrived in Jammu and Kashmir which will visit multiple flood hit districts in next two days. The team is headed by a Joint Secretary (F-II) ranked officer of Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India and is comprising of officers from other Ministeries including Ministry of Roads, Transport and Highways, Power Department, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Rural Development, Ministry of Jal Shakti Department and Department of Space, GoI. Official sources said that the team will be split in two sub-teams with one team will be deputed to districts of Chenab valley including Doda and Kishtwar while another team will be visiting Rajouri and Poonch districts. The sub-team deputed to Rajouri and Poonch has already arrived in Rajouri district with senior officers of district administration are accompanying the team which is scheduled to visit various flood hit areas where devastation in floods happened in this year's flood. Official sources stated that the team will examine post flood situation after which it will submit a detailed report before Government of India based on which financial packages will be sanctioned. Earlier, on Tuesday, during visit of Rajouri, Chief Secretary Dr. Sajjan Singh Yadav also told media persons that a high level inter-ministerial team is visiting areas of Jammu and Kashmir. " Central team is visiting Jammu and Kashmir tomorrow which will conduct visit of flood hit areas after which financial package will be given to us by which we will be able to compensate the losses of victims and will also pace up rebuilding of necessary infrastructure." CS had said.

stories.headline: Why has the INDIA bloc posed 48 questions to the Election Commission over SIR?
stories.title: Why has the INDIA bloc posed 48 questions to the Election Commission over SIR?
stories.summary: Through the interrogatories, the petitioners want the decision making process to be made public
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Supreme Court’s decision to hear an application by Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and other Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) bloc leaders seeking leave to deliver 48 interrogatories to the Election Commission of India (ECI) has added a new dimension to the legal challenge against the nationwide Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
The questions seek to establish how the exercise was authorised, whether the Commission acted collectively and who approved changes to voter registration procedures and digital systems.
The Opposition leaders have challenged the manner in which the nationwide SIR was initiated and conducted in a writ petition under Article 32 of the Constitution.

They allege that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar exercised the Commission’s collective powers without the knowledge or concurrence of Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

They have also questioned the absence of a recorded decision authorising the exercise, an additional declaration introduced in online Form 6, and the functioning of the ECINET and ERONET electoral databases.

In its counter-affidavit of October 26, the ECI said the SIR orders of June 24, 2025, October 27, 2025 and May 14, 2026, and the decision to file the affidavit, had been approved unanimously by all three members.
In his rejoinder, Mr. Gandhi questioned the absence of minutes, file notings or other records supporting this claim.

stories.headline: SC cancels HC order asking CBI, ED to probe DA claims against Rahul Gandhi
stories.title: SC cancels HC order asking CBI, ED to probe DA claims against Rahul Gandhi
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 25 : The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside the Allahabad High Court order, which directed the CBI and the ED to verify allegations of disproportionate assets against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana remitted the petition filed by BJP member Vignesh Shishir to the high court for fresh consideration, including the question of maintainability. The top court had earlier asked the Allahabad High Court not to proceed with a case involving allegations of disproportionate assets against the Congress leader. It had also asked the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Enforcement Directorate (ED) not to file any report in pursuance of the directions of the high court in the case lodged against the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha. Gandhi earlier moved the Supreme Court challenging the high court order with the directions to the CBI and ED. The high court had noted that the affidavit filed by the CBI was not in compliance with its earlier order and did not adequately explain the progress made on the complaint submitted by the petitioner against Gandhi related to his assets. The court had directed the joint director or the head of the zone concerned at the CBI's Anti-Corruption division's headquarters in New Delhi to personally file a fresh affidavit, detailing the progress made in the matter. The BJP leader had earlier filed pleas also alleging that the Congress leader held dual citizenship. PTI

stories.headline: Supreme Court Reserves Judgment On Balwant Singh Rajoana's Plea To Commute Death Sentence Over Delay In Mercy Petition
stories.title: Supreme Court Reserves Judgment On Balwant Singh Rajoana's Plea To Commute Death Sentence Over Delay In Mercy Petition
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday reserved judgment on a plea filed by Babbar Khalsa terrorist Balwant Singh Rajoana seeking commutation of his death sentence in the assassination of former Punjab Chief Minister Beant Singh, citing the prolonged delay in deciding his mercy petition pending before the President since 2012.
A bench of Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Sandeep Mehta, and Justice Aparesh Singh reserved judgment.

Today, Senior Advocate Mukul Rohatgi for Rajoana argued that the Supreme Court's May 2023 judgment, which declined to commute his death sentence at that stage, left the competent authority free to consider the mercy petition in due course.
However, he submitted, nearly three-and-a-half years have since passed without a decision.
Rohatgi also referred to Rajoana's nearly 30 years of incarceration and argued that the delay continues to affect his rights under Article 21 of the Constitution.
Additional Solicitor General KM Nataraj opposed the plea, arguing that Rajoana himself did not file the mercy petition and that the representation came from another person.
He submitted that Article 21 could not be invoked on the basis of a mercy petition filed by someone else which has remained pending.

Nataraj also referred to Rajoana's statements during the trial expressing lack of faith in the Constitution and the judicial system, arguing that he could not now seek relief by invoking constitutional provisions.
He further submitted that the circumstances in Punjab, which the Court considered in its earlier judgment, had not undergone any substantial change.

The ASG also relied on the 2025 Constitution Bench opinion in the Presidential reference concerning the powers of Governors and the President over State Bills and argued that the relief could not be granted by invoking Article 142, as Article 142 cannot substitute the constitutional powers of remission under Articles 72 and 161.

Rohatgi pointed out that Rajoana has approached the court under Article 32, and countered that Article 21 remains available even to a person who earlier expressed distrust in the constitutional system.
He argued that Rajoana's earlier refusal to pursue an appeal could not permanently deprive him of constitutional remedies.

stories.headline: Delhi riots: SC issues notice to Delhi Police on pleas by Sharjeel Imam, Umar Khalid seeking bail
stories.title: Delhi riots: SC issues notice to Delhi Police on pleas by Sharjeel Imam, Umar Khalid seeking bail
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 25: The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused, as of now, interim bail to activists Sharjeel Imam and Umar Khalid, who had challenged a Delhi High Court order denying them bail in a UAPA case related to the alleged "larger conspiracy" behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice to the Delhi Police and sought its response. During the hearing, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Khalid, sought interim bail in the meantime. Senior Advocate Siddharth Dave, appearing for Imam, also sought similar relief on grounds of long incarceration. However, the bench said, "Not today". It said it will hear the police before considering the prayer for interim bail. The top court also directed that the matter be placed before the CJI on the administrative side for constitution of a three-judge bench for consideration. In their pleas before the top court, the activists have sought bail, contending that the prosecution has failed to examine protected witnesses and that the one-year embargo imposed by the Supreme Court is nearing its expiry. Violence erupted in northeast Delhi during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), 2019, and the National Register of Citizens (NRC). Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.

stories.headline: IPL 2027 auction sees 1,220 registrations from Indian, foreign players
stories.title: IPL 2027 auction sees 1,220 registrations from Indian, foreign players
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 25 : A whopping 1,220 players have been named in the IPL 2027 Auction Register, the tournament's statement said on Wednesday. The list includes 939 Indians and 281 overseas players, but only 66 of them can secure contracts when franchises bid in the auction to be held in Goa on December 16. The ten franchises have already retained 184 players ahead of the auction, and no more than 25 of the open slots can go to overseas cricketers. The register is heavily tilted towards uncapped talent, with 994 players who have not played international cricket registering for it. The rest are 184 capped players and 42 cricketers from Associate nations. The list is divided into six categories. Capped internationals are at 170, and capped Indians are at 14. The other four are the 42 Associate players, the 127 uncapped Indians with IPL experience, the 798 uncapped Indians who have never featured in the league before and the 69 uncapped overseas players. Australia has the most overseas players on the register, with 53 representatives. South Africa have 40, while West Indies 36, New Zealand 25, Afghanistan 23 and Sri Lanka 21 players respectively. England followed with 16, Bangladesh with 12, Ireland with seven and Zimbabwe with six, respectively. Thirteen players from the USA are on the register, the most from any Associate nation. The UAE and Nepal have 10 each, the Netherlands three, and Canada, Japan and Scotland two each. The franchises have Rs 295.60 crore left between them for the auction, after spending Rs 1,004.40 crore so far. Lucknow Super Giants have the most money left, at Rs 47.45 crore, and seven slots to fill. Gujarat Titans have the least, with Rs 8.75 crore and only three openings. Delhi Capitals (Rs 39.50 crore) and Mumbai Indians (Rs 30.25 crore) need nine players each, the most of any team. Kolkata Knight Riders have eight slots to fill with Rs 41.65 crore, and Sunrisers Hyderabad have seven slots to fill with Rs 40.15 crore. Chennai Super Kings, Rajasthan Royals and Punjab Kings each need six players, with budgets of Rs 28.05 crore, Rs 27.05 crore and Rs 18.60 crore, respectively. Defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru have Rs 14.15 crore to fill five places. DC also have to fill four overseas slots, the most of any team, while RCB have only one foreign player to sign up. The franchises will now tell the tournament organisers which players from the register they want in the final auction pool. The final Auction List and player sets will be released on December 4. ( IANS)

stories.headline: Cabinet clears Rs 2,014-crore Greenfield airport project in Assam
stories.title: Cabinet clears Rs 2,014-crore Greenfield airport project in Assam
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 25:T o overcome the severe operational and spatial constraints of the existing defense landlocked civil enclave at Silchar Airport and to accommodate sustained passenger growth, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs chaired by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has approved the development of a New Greenfield Airport at Doloo, Silchar, Assam by the Airports Authority of India (AAI) at an estimated cost of Rs.2,014 crore. Doloo, situated in the Cachar District of Assam, serves as the strategic heart of the Barak Valley—a region renowned for its extensive tea gardens, agro-based industries, and immense potential for eco and cultural tourism. The proposed Terminal Building will span a total area of 12,351 sqm with a capacity to handle 800 passengers during peak hour, designed with modern passenger amenities, sustainable green building principles, and modular expansion capability. In addition, the project encompasses the development of a 2,705m x 45m, Code-4C compliant runway suitable for A-320 aircraft operations, along with the construction of a new Apron capable of parking 6 nos. A-320 aircraft and a dedicated isolation bay. As a project of immense strategic significance, the Doloo Greenfield Airport will meet the rapidly growing demands of air traffic in South Assam and adjoining areas of neighbouring States. It will significantly decongest existing infrastructure, unlock regional economic potential by boosting trade and tourism, and offer a world-class gateway integrating Northeast India with broader national and international growth corridors.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves continuation of Estates Management Scheme for Department of Posts with an outlay of Rs 1,491 crore
stories.title: Cabinet approves continuation of Estates Management Scheme for Department of Posts with an outlay of Rs 1,491 crore
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 25: The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has approved the proposal of the Department of Posts for the continuation of the Central Sector Scheme, the Estates Management Scheme, during the 16th Finance Commission Cycle from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. The scheme carries a total financial outlay of Rs.1,491 crores over a five-year period. The scheme aims to comprehensively transform and modernize the estates infrastructure of the Department of Posts. It focuses heavily on the construction, re-construction, renovation, uniform branding of post offices and residential colonies, along with the preservation of India’s heritage postal buildings. This modernization strategy directly supports first-mile delivery, fosters financial inclusion and enhances citizen centric service delivery nationwide, aligning with the broader visions of Digital India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat. As one of the world's largest postal networks with 1.65 lakh post offices (including 1,49,385 in rural areas), India Post remains a critical vehicle for mails, banking (POSB/IPPB), insurance (PLI), Aadhaar services, Post Office Passport Seva Kendras and rural artisan support via Dakghar Niryat Kendras (DNKs). The scheme is scheduled for phased implementation over a five-year horizon, starting from FY 2026-27 through FY 2030-31. Key Components of the Approved Scheme: New Construction (Rs. 280 Crore): Building 190 departmental postal buildings on vacant departmental plots to replace currently rented spaces and eliminate rental liabilities. Re-construction (Rs. 108 Crore): Demolishing and rebuilding 50 dilapidated departmental postal structures to ensure long-term structural safety. Renovation & Branding (Rs. 318 Crore): Upgrading and establishing uniform branding across 2,550 departmental SubPost Offices as per SPA guidelines. Rented Post Office Upgrades (Rs. 37.50 Crore): Upgrading and uniformly branding 2,500 post offices operating out of rented premises. Heritage Preservation (Rs. 180 Crore): Restoring and preserving 20 landmark heritage postal buildings to safeguard the historical legacy of the department. Colony Renovation (Rs. 357.50 Crore): Revamping 150 high demand postal residential colonies to elevate employee welfare and satisfaction. Allied & Inclusive Activities (Rs. 100 Crore): Implementing sustainable features (Solar power, Rainwater Harvesting) and universal accessibility infrastructure (ramps, Braille signage) under the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan, alongwith gender-focused additions like ladies toilets and feeding rooms. Integrated Technology Center (Rs. 100 Crore): Setting up a permanent physical infrastructure for the Centre for Excellence in Postal Technology (CEPT) in Bengaluru to drive Advanced Postal Technology (APT) services and support the indigenous Opensource Tech Stack.

stories.title: Supreme Court Dismisses IDBI Officers' Challenge To Pension Scheme Noting Union's Move To Sell IDBI Stakes To Canadian Entity
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has dismissed the appeals concerning IDBI Bank's pension scheme after noting the Union Government's approval of the strategic sale of a 60.72% stake in the bank to a subsidiary of Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd.

A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran observed that, given the Centre's decision to proceed with the strategic disinvestment, “there is nothing much, we can do in the matter(s).” The Court, however, kept open the appellants' right to pursue appropriate legal remedies before the competent forum.

The Court was informed about a Ministry of Finance press release dated October 14, 2026, announcing that the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs had approved M/s 10955230 Canada Inc., whose parent entity is Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd., as the strategic buyer of an aggregate 60.72% equity stake in IDBI Bank.
The proposed transaction involves the sale of the Government of India's 30.48% stake and LIC's 30.24% stake in IDBI Bank.
Upon completion of the transaction, the Government and LIC would retain 15% and 19% stakes, respectively.
The Cabinet Committee has also authorised the sale of the Government's residual 15% stake through the open market.
The press release clarified that the successful bidder was yet to present its credentials before the Reserve Bank of India and submit a roadmap for compliance with applicable regulatory conditions.
The appeals were filed by the All India IDBI.

Officers Association and other appellants challenging the Bombay High Court's decision to dismiss their writ petitions on the ground that IDBI Bank was not 'State' under Article 12 of the Constitution and was therefore not amenable to writ jurisdiction under Article 226.
The Supreme Court agreed with the High Court's view that IDBI was not 'State'.

The officers' association had challenged an IDBI Bank circular dated April 18, 2012, seeking an additional opportunity for employees who had not earlier opted for the IDBI Defined Benefit Pension Scheme.
It had also questioned retrospective deductions from employees' salaries towards pension contributions under the New Pension Scheme from April 1, 2008.

stories.headline: Kolkata Municipal Polls Shouldn't Be Unreasonably Deferred : Supreme Court Proposes Shifting Delimitation Challenge To HC Division Bench
stories.title: Kolkata Municipal Polls Shouldn't Be Unreasonably Deferred : Supreme Court Proposes Shifting Delimitation Challenge To HC Division Bench
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday proposed to set aside the Calcutta High Court's order which deferred the Kolkata Municipal Corporation elections till a challenge to delimitation of wards is decided.

Orally observing elections should not be deferred "unreasonably", the Court proposed to transfer the challenge to delimitation from the single bench to the division bench of the High Court for a faster decision.

Hearing a petition filed by the West Bengal government challenging the High Court's order, the Court suggested that the Division Bench order can be set aside for a fresh consideration, and until the issues are considered afresh, the election notification can be withheld.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana proposed to Solicitor General Tushar Mehta (for WB) and Senior Advocates Dr AM Singhvi and Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya (for respondents) that it could set aside the Division Bench's interim order and relegate the matter back to the High Court for a fresh consideration by a Division Bench, not a Single Bench.
The bench noted that all factual and legal issues raised by the State had not been considered by the High Court in the impugned decision.
During the hearing, Justice Bagchi remarked that the elections should not be unreasonably deferred.
Both sides will come back with instructions on Monday.
The dispute concerns the West Bengal Government's decision to increase the number of wards in the Kolkata Municipal Corporation from 144 to 209 ahead of the municipal elections.
The State Government issued a delimitation notification on September 11, 2026, redrawing the boundaries of the municipal wards.
The exercise was challenged before the Calcutta High Court on the ground that it was undertaken without a valid recommendation from the elected Municipal Corporation.

The petitioners questioned the authority of Smita Pandey, who had been appointed Administrator of the KMC after the elected Corporation ceased to function, to make the recommendation for delimitation.
They argued that an Administrator could not substitute the elected Municipal Corporation for the purpose of making such a recommendation.

stories.headline: Supreme Court sets aside Karnataka HC order suspending Vinay Kulkarni's life sentence in BJP leader murder case
stories.title: Supreme Court sets aside Karnataka HC order suspending Vinay Kulkarni's life sentence in BJP leader murder case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: New Delhi: Former Karnataka minister Vinay Kulkarni, convicted of murdering a BJP leader in 2016, could be headed back to prison with the Supreme Court on Wednesday setting aside the high court order that stayed his conviction and suspended his life term sentence.

An apex court bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar also set aside the order suspending the sentences of other convicts, including Kulkarni's maternal uncle Chandrashekhar Indi alias Chandu Mama and investigating officer in the case Channakeshava B Tingarikar.
Dharwad BJP leader Yogesh Goudar was hacked to death by an armed group at a gymnasium in the city in June 2016.
Kulkarni and 15 others were convicted by the Special Court for MPs and MLAs in Bengaluru on April 16 this year.
The court sentenced them to life imprisonment a day later.
On July 31, the Karnataka High Court stayed Kulkarni's conviction in the case and suspended the life sentence.
It also ordered Kulkarni's release on bail pending disposal of his appeal.
The Dharwad bench of the high court directed him to execute a personal bond of Rs 5 lakh with two sureties of the like amount.
It barred Kulkarni from leaving the country without prior permission and directed the ex-MLA to appear before the high court and the trial court, whenever required.
The probe into the case was handed over to the CBI in 2019.
Kulkarni, who was a minister when the murder took place, was arrested by the CBI in 2020 and was later granted bail before being convicted by the special court earlier this year.

stories.headline: NSA Doval calls for closer regional security cooperation to counter challenges in Indian Ocean
stories.title: NSA Doval calls for closer regional security cooperation to counter challenges in Indian Ocean
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 25: India remains committed to working closely with key Indian Ocean nations to enhance their collective capacities to deal with evolving security threats, National Security Advisor Ajit Doval said on Wednesday. In his address at the eighth Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) in Male, Doval listed various pressing challenges facing the region and called for deeper strategic cooperation to address them. The CSC has emerged as a key regional security grouping of Indian Ocean littoral states, comprising India, Sri Lanka, the Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh, and Seychelles. It has largely been focusing on maritime safety, counter-terrorism, and transnational security cooperation. "The Colombo Security Conclave represents the intersection of our Neighborhood First outlook and the MAHASAGAR vision," Doval said. "We are committed to continue working closely with the CSC countries to enhance our collective capacities in dealing with the evolving serious security challenges," he added. Last March, during his visit to Mauritius, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the vision MAHASAGAR, or 'Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions, for India's engagement with the Global South. Doval said he was confident that the CSC will become an effective instrument in the Indian Ocean region to provide collective security and look after common interests. "India has been trying to work very closely with Sri Lanka, with the Maldives and other countries, and we want to see that this cooperation is further extended," the NSA said. "I assure all of you that India, as one of the countries which had initiated the idea of the Colombo Security Conclave, will give its best and will try to give all necessary help, assistance. I assure you of our fullest commitment to achieve our common objectives," Doval added. The Colombo Security Conclave was established in 2020 when India, Sri Lanka and Maldives agreed to expand the scope and membership of their trilateral meeting on maritime cooperation. Cooperation under the CSC focuses on the five pillars of maritime safety and security, countering terrorism and radicalisation, combating trafficking and transnational organised crime and cyber security, protection of critical infrastructure, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.
